newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's PCS starts up new ethylene plant.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's PCS starts up new ethylene plant.

text.p: The Petrochemical Corporation of Singapore (PCS) is starting up its new 515,000-tonnes-per-year ethylene plant on Wednesday, a company spokeswoman said.
"We are in the process of starting up the plant," she said.
Industry sources said the unit will commence production at a rate of 70 to 80-percent and will slowly increase to full commercial production by June, with the official opening only slated for August.
Sources said the company will not be able to raise production to full capacity sooner as one of its key endusers will only start up its own plant in the middle of the year.

PCS, a 50:50 joint venture between Royal Dutch Shell and a consortium of Japanese companies, already operates a 450,000-tonnes-per-year ethylene plant at Pulau Ayer Merbau, one of a group of small islands off the southern coast of Singapore.

Late last year, managing director Takayuki Okada told Reuters that 80-percent of naphtha feedstock required for the new plant had already been secured on term, with 10-percent from the Mideast and the remainder from Singapore.
The new plant will expand PCS's annual more than double the company's requirements to 2.5 million tonnes-per-year (62,000-barrels-per-day) from around one million.
